============================================================
                    EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
============================================================

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy: Randomized-Controlled Trial (RCT) estimated with an ANCOVA / Difference-in-Means framework, supplemented with Difference-in-Differences (DID) when pre-project baseline observations are available.

Why appropriate?
• External audits were randomly assigned by the government. Randomization, by construction, breaks the correlation between potential outcomes and treatment.  
• ANCOVA (regressing the post-audit outcome on treatment and baseline outcome/covariates) delivers the most efficient unbiased estimate under random assignment (McKenzie 2012).  
• If the data include a pre-implementation observation of corruption (e.g., engineering cost estimates taken before payments start), DID provides additional precision and allows us to test for pre-treatment balance.  
• In the presence of imperfect compliance (some assigned villages never actually receive an audit), assignment can be used as an instrument for “audit actually conducted” in a two-stage least squares (CACE / LATE).

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable:  
   treat_it = 1 if village-project i in fiscal year t was *randomly assigned* to receive an external audit (Intention-To-Treat), 0 otherwise.  
   compl_it  = 1 if an audit actually took place (Received-Treatment).

Control group (counterfactual):  
   Village-projects that were *not* selected for an audit in the same fiscal year.

Treatment timing / event date:  
   Randomization occurs ex-ante (typically at the beginning of fiscal year t). Audits are conducted part-way through project execution. Outcomes (measured corruption) are observed at project completion.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Random assignment:  P(treat_it | X) = P(treat_it)  
    – Plausible; assignment performed by central government lottery.

A2. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) / No spillovers:  
    – Needs scrutiny. Contractors that operate in both treatment and control villages could transfer knowledge. Spatial separation of villages and use of different contractors make large spillovers unlikely but not impossible.

A3. Non-differential measurement:  The way corruption is *measured* must not differ systematically between treatment and control.  
    – Plausible if corruption is calculated from engineering surveys independent of the audit team. If audit reports themselves provide the outcome, the assumption is violated (auditors naturally find more). We will therefore construct the main outcome from **third-party engineering quantity surveys** collected uniformly across all villages.

A4. No attrition / selective sample loss:  
    – The project data are administrative; very low attrition expected. We will verify equal completion rates across arms.

A5. For IV (CACE): Exclusion & monotonicity  
    – Assignment affects outcomes only through the presence of an audit, and assignment does not *prevent* audits in treatment villages (no “defiers”). Both are plausible.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Spillovers / contamination  
    • Test: Compare outcomes for control villages that are geographically close (<10 km) to treated villages against those farther away.  
    • Mitigate: Cluster SEs at the sub-district level; run robustness excluding close neighbors.

T2. Non-compliance (some treated villages never actually audited; or controls audited by other agencies)  
    • Mitigate:  
        – Report ITT as primary.  
        – Estimate CACE using 2SLS with assignment as instrument for actual audit.  
        – Provide first-stage F-statistic and compliance rates.

T3. Audit-generated information bias (audits detect corruption that otherwise stays hidden, mechanically raising measured corruption in treated villages)  
    • Solution: Use *independent engineering re-measurement* (material inputs, physical progress) as the corruption metric rather than discrepancies raised in the audit report itself.  
    • Sensitivity: Show that results hold when the outcome is (Funds allocated ‑ engineer-verified spending) / Funds allocated.

5. R CODE OUTLINE
------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-performance FE / IV regressions
library(estimatr)     # randomization inference
library(sandwich)     # robust SEs

# ---- 1. Load data ----
dt <- fread("indo_village_projects.csv")

# ---- 2. Construct variables ----
# Corruption share: fraction of funds unaccounted for in independent engineering survey
dt[, corrupt_share := (funds_allocated - engineer_verified_spending) / funds_allocated]

# Treatment dummies
dt[, treat := as.integer(assignment_audit == 1)]        # ITT
dt[, audit_real := as.integer(actual_audit == 1)]       # Received treatment

# Baseline corruption (pre-project engineer estimate)
dt[, corrupt_pre := shift(corrupt_share, n = 1, type = "lead"), by = village_id]  # example

# ---- 3. Main ITT specification (ANCOVA) ----
# Y_it = β0 + β1 * treat_it + β2 * corrupt_pre + δ_district + ε_it
fe_itt <- feols(corrupt_share ~ treat + corrupt_pre | district_id, 
                data = dt, cluster = "district_id")
summary(fe_itt)

# ---- 4. CACE / IV for non-compliance ----
fe_iv <- feols(corrupt_share ~ 1 | district_id | 
               audit_real ~ treat + corrupt_pre, 
               data = dt, cluster = "district_id")
summary(fe_iv)

# ---- 5. Robustness: Spillover check ----
# Create distance to nearest treated village
# (Assume pre-computed 'dist_to_nearest_treated')  
dt[, near_treat := dist_to_nearest_treated < 10]  # indicator

fe_spill <- feols(corrupt_share ~ treat + near_treat + corrupt_pre | district_id, 
                  data = dt, cluster = "district_id")
summary(fe_spill)

# ---- 6. Randomization inference for ITT ----
ri_itt <- permtest(fe_itt, treatment = "treat", sims = 1000)
ri_itt$p.value
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS
------------------------------------------------------------
Prior: External audits *reduce* missing expenditures.  
Magnitude: Baseline missing share ≈ 25 % of allocated funds. Expect a decline of 7–10 percentage points (≈30–40 % reduction). The CACE estimate (effect on audited projects) may be slightly larger than ITT if compliance <100 %.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (1 = satisfied, 0 = questionable)
------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Successful randomization & balance checks ..................... 1  
C2: No interference / spillovers .................................. 0.5  
C3: Low attrition & equal data quality across groups .............. 1  
C4: Outcome not directly affected by audit measurement process .... 0.5  
C5: Correct statistical inference (cluster at assignment level) ... 1  
Total (out of 5) = 4.0

============================================================
